name: Dremio
license: Proprietary (Dremio Cloud and Enterprise); the free Community Edition is Apache 2.0 (dremio-oss), last released as 26.0.5 in September 2025
summary: A SQL lakehouse engine built on Apache Arrow, with its own Iceberg catalog and “reflections” that speed up queries without anyone changing them.
intro: A Dremio cluster has a coordinator and one or more engines made of executors. The coordinator plans each SQL query with a cost-based optimizer, and the executors read Parquet, Iceberg and Delta Lake data straight from S3, Azure or Google Cloud Storage into Apache Arrow buffers and process it there, keeping hot data in a columnar cache on their local disks. The same query can also reach databases such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake or MongoDB, so you can join lake tables with live systems. Analysts build views on top, and Dremio can back any table or view with a reflection: a precomputed copy, raw or pre-aggregated, stored as an Iceberg table. Queries keep naming the original view; the optimizer rewrites them to use a reflection when that plan is cheaper, and reflections on Iceberg tables refresh themselves when the table changes. BI tools connect over JDBC, ODBC or Arrow Flight SQL.

Since version 26.0 (April 2025), Dremio ships Open Catalog, a built-in Iceberg catalog based on Apache Polaris, which Dremio co-created. It speaks the Iceberg REST protocol, so Spark, Flink or Kafka Connect can write tables that Dremio then serves. There are three editions. Dremio Cloud is fully managed on AWS and bills $0.20 per Dremio Compute Unit (DCU); the smallest engine uses 16 DCUs an hour ($3.20) and a Medium 128 ($25.60), counted per second with a 60-second minimum (prices checked October 6, 2026). Dremio Enterprise is self-managed on Kubernetes with consumption pricing set by sales. The free Community Edition lacks the catalog, access control and Autonomous Reflections, and its open-source code hasn’t been updated since September 2025. SAP completed its purchase of Dremio on July 6, 2026.
strengths: Reflections speed up dashboards without changing their SQL: the optimizer substitutes them, and Enterprise and Cloud can create and drop them automatically from query patterns
Open formats end to end: Iceberg tables, Parquet files and a Polaris-based REST catalog that other engines can read and write
Federation: one query can join Iceberg tables with PostgreSQL, Oracle, Snowflake, MongoDB and other live sources
Arrow-native from storage to client: Arrow Flight SQL and an ADBC-based Power BI connector return columns without row-by-row conversion
limits: The open-source Community Edition is falling behind: `dremio-oss` stopped at 26.0.5 (September 2025) while Enterprise moved to 26.1.x, and it has no role-based access control, hosted catalog or built-in monitoring metrics
SAP bought Dremio in 2026; SAP has pledged to keep contributing to Iceberg, Polaris and Arrow, but its announcements don’t say how standalone Dremio will be sold in future
Dremio Cloud is AWS only for now (Azure is listed as coming soon); Enterprise pricing isn’t published
Reflections are extra copies: they use storage and engine time to refresh, and on Cloud that refresh time is billed in DCUs like queries
Autonomous Reflections only cover Iceberg tables, Parquet datasets and views on them, and are capped at 100 reflections, 10 new per day

snippet.title: An Iceberg table, a federated view and a reflection that speeds it up
source: -- an Iceberg table in Open Catalog, partitioned by day
order_id BIGINT, customer_id BIGINT, country VARCHAR, amount DECIMAL(10,2), ts TIMESTAMP)
-- a view that joins it with a live PostgreSQL table; nothing is copied
SELECT o.country, c.segment, CAST(o.ts AS DATE) AS order_day, o.amount
JOIN crm_pg.public.customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id;
-- a precomputed aggregate that Dremio maintains
-- dashboards still query the view; the planner uses the reflection
WHERE order_day >= DATE '2026-09-01' GROUP BY country;

items.name: Trino
items.text: Open-source SQL engine with many connectors that streams data between workers in memory. Its Iceberg connector has materialized views you refresh with `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`, and the catalog comes from elsewhere (Glue, a REST catalog, Polaris).

items.name: Amazon Athena
items.text: Serverless Trino-based SQL over S3 with the Glue catalog. Nothing to run and $5 per TB scanned on demand, so repeated dashboard scans add up; Iceberg tables must live in the Glue catalog.

story: Tomer Shiran, who had led product at MapR, Microsoft and IBM, and Jacques Nadeau, who ran MapR’s distributed systems team and was vice president of Apache Drill, founded Dremio in Mountain View in 2015. Their goal, in the company’s words, was to let analysts get the data they need “from any data source, then accelerate analytical processing for BI tools, machine learning, data science, and SQL clients.”

Nadeau wanted a standard in-memory columnar format so systems could stop converting data between them. That idea became Apache Arrow, launched as an Apache top-level project in February 2016 with Nadeau as its vice president, and Dremio’s engine reads every source straight into Arrow buffers. Dremio published its source under Apache 2.0 in July 2017, and version 2.0 in April 2018 extended Data Reflections, its acceleration layer.

Dremio later recast itself as an Iceberg lakehouse platform. It co-created Apache Polaris, an open Iceberg catalog, and 26.0 in April 2025 shipped a catalog built on it along with Autonomous Reflections. SAP announced in May 2026 that it would buy Dremio to combine SAP and non-SAP data for AI, and completed the deal on July 6.

choices.choice: Arrow buffers from end to end
choices.why: Converting rows between formats wasted CPU in every hop. Reading each source into Arrow, processing in Arrow and returning Arrow over Flight removes those conversions.

Users query tables and views, never the reflections. The optimizer compares plans with and without each reflection and picks the cheaper one, so acceleration can be added or dropped without changing dashboards.
Instead of loading everything into a warehouse first, Dremio connects to object stores and databases and joins them in one query, with views as a shared semantic layer.
Dremio says it co-created Polaris “because organizations demanded an open alternative to proprietary catalogs like AWS Glue and Unity Catalog”, so other engines can share the same tables.

timeline.text: Founded by Tomer Shiran and Jacques Nadeau in Mountain View
Apache Arrow launched in February, with Nadeau as vice president
Source code published under Apache 2.0 in July (release 1.0.8)
